The resulting 9.32 TB release includes wheel geometries, vehicle and component force coefficients, accumulated drag, surface pressure, wall shear stress, and flow fields around the vehicle and wheels. Together, these data support surrogate model training and evaluation across diverse rim geometries, as well as aerodynamic optimisation and generative design to accelerate wheel rim development for vehicle drag reduction.

title: What Matters for LLM Persona Simulation: Signal Form in Cold-Start E-Commerce Advertising
summary: Estimating advertising performance in cold-start settings is challenging because historical logs are unavailable before launch. Large language models (LLMs) offer a potential alternative by simulating persona-conditioned user responses, but it remains unclear which design choices actually drive LLM-based persona simulation. Using real Google Ads e-commerce campaign data across five demographic segments, we identify three signal-form dimensions that affect simulation quality: (i) a demographic anchor without noisy rich attributes, (ii) a relative qualitative banner-blindness signal rather than quantitative anchors, and (iii) prompt phrasing. On this campaign, our method attains an MAE of 24.9 and a MAPE of 26.1%, a 51.3% lower MAE than the best tested non-LLM baseline and 77.3% lower than an LLM configuration using explicit CTR anchors. Systematic ablations show that minimal demographic descriptions achieve lower mean error than richer persona configurations, while relative qualitative cues substantially outperform the tested quantitative anchors. We additionally compare these configurations with direct-prior and rule-based baselines and with alternative LLM configurations.

title: Containment Problems in Convex Sets
summary: Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane, and let $C$ be a compact, convex subset of the plane that contains the origin in its interior. We study the problem of finding two points $p$ and $q$ of $P$ with the property that any homothet of $C$ that contains $p$ and $q$ must contain at least a constant fraction of the points of $P$. We give proofs for several cases. When $C$ is strictly convex we achieve a fraction of $1/5$, and when $C$ is a general convex region we achieve a fraction of $1/6e$. We show how the ideas of this second bound can be used to prove a lower bound for a version of the problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $C$ is a $d$-ball. We also consider a few special cases. When $C$ is a triangle we get a lower bound of $1/12$, and when we allow that triangle to be rotated by $π$ radians in addition to being scaled and translated we get a lower bound of $1/768$. In proving this last result, we improve the state of the art on the version of this problem in three dimensions, where $C$ is a parallelepiped. We also consider the algorithmic aspects of finding such a pair of points.

title: Notwithstanding Anything to the Contrary, Ignore All Instructions: Measuring Prompt Injection Guards on Legal Contract Review Attacks
summary: Specialized prompt injection guards are deployed in front of document analysis systems, but no false positive rate has been published for any of them on legal contracts. We measure eleven open-weights guards on two corpora of legal contracts and find that existing guards struggle: document-level false positive rates are as high as 92.39%; two guards fall below chance on paired AUC; and a five-regex baseline is not Pareto-dominated by any guard in the panel. Controlled probes locate model-specific as well as general failure modes. Prompted LLMs resolve the tested failures, including a second threat category (unauthorized scope claims) on which every guard scores zero. A cascaded LLM solution, where the positives of a mid-tier model are verified by a frontier model, is 6.5x cheaper than using exclusively a frontier model and approaches its performance.

title: Protein B-factor modeling with local magnitude
summary: Topological magnitude characterizes the effective size and spatial organization of metric spaces, offering a geometric approach with potential applications in molecular biology and materials science. Previous work has demonstrated its utility in modeling protein flexibility from structure, but global magnitude weighting requires dense linear systems whose computational cost increases with protein size. We introduce a local magnitude representation that retains residue-level structural information through nearest-neighbor environments. The construction is well posed and geometrically invariant, with central weighting distinguished from scalar neighborhood magnitude. Across 364 proteins, the mean within-protein fitting Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) increases from 0.725 for global magnitude to 0.728 for local magnitude. Blind-prediction experiments on 345 proteins combine each representation with identical auxiliary descriptors and evaluate random forests and gradient boosting under three validation protocols. Local features improve the primary PCC in all six model--protocol comparisons, with a maximum absolute increase of 0.008 in protein-level ten-fold gradient boosting. For a fixed feature bank, local factorization costs $O(Nk^3)$ compared with $O(N^3)$ for global factorization, where $N$ is the number of C$_α$ atoms and $k$ the neighborhood size. Timing measurements show a computational advantage of local magnitude on large structures. Within the tested single-seed configuration and distinct global and local scale banks, these results support local magnitude as a compact representation that preserves useful B-factor information while reducing feature-extraction costs for large proteins.

title: Global Solar Siting from Geospatial Embeddings
summary: Global solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity is rapidly growing, helping decrease our emissions and dependence on fossil fuels. However, optimally siting a solar plant remains challenging, requiring anticipation of geographical, urban, and infrastructure needs. Current methods rely on multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) using hand-picked geophysical layers and solar-resource products, however these strategies are not geographically transferable and do not capture the practical requirements of solar sites. We use geospatial embeddings, dense vectors representing geophysical properties of a location, to analyse 38,591 existing solar sites and the land they were built on to learn the latent solar suitability signal. We assess a set of linear and non-linear models and select a soft-voting ensemble of a random forest and a multilayer perceptron (RF+MLP ensemble), chosen for accuracy and large scale deployability. Validated against future installations in thirteen countries, the ensemble separates existing solar sites from random land with a median ROC-AUC of 0.90. Compared with published MCDA strategies, the ensemble increases ROC-AUC by 0.06-0.30 in every country. The ranking also concentrates real deployment: the most-suitable 20% of land holds 84% of estimated generation (annual energy yield) and 67% of installed capacity (potential power output). After applying standard siting constraints, 5.6% of global land (9.8% if cropland is permitted) remains highly suited to solar. The global 10 m resolution solar suitability dataset and code can be found here: https://github.com/Abdullahr29/Global-Solar-Siting.

title: Safety Direction Adapter: A Training-Free Post-Hoc Safety Patch for Fine-Tuned Open-Weight LLMs
summary: Open-weight LLMs are routinely fine-tuned from public repositories, yet task-specific adaptation can silently erode safety alignment inherited from instruct-tuned bases. This is a supply-chain risk when organizations ship third-party checkpoints without full re-alignment. Prior work rarely audits diverse public fine-tunes under a shared multi-axis safety-utility protocol or offers training-free mitigation at deployment time. We propose Safety Direction Adapter (SDA), a training-free post-hoc safety patch that extracts a safety direction once from an aligned base and transfers it one-to-many within that base family as a small PEFT-compatible weight update, evaluated under the same multi-axis protocol. Across six direction extractors, we evaluate 14 checkpoints from two 1-2B lineages and probe 8B and 27B fleets (n=5 each) on 15 benchmarks (12538 prompts). On Llama, SDA improves the four-axis mean by about 2.3 points against a 4.2-point instruct-relative gap (about 55 percent recovery; partial Avg), with Safety and Cyber recovering toward or beyond instruct; Safety gains about 8.5 points against about 4.9 points mean degradation. On Qwen, degradation is larger and excess-driven; SDA still lifts Avg (about 36 percent of the gap) while trading Safety and Cyber against Excess and General. We report dual-use risks of publishing direction adapters and do not claim robustness to adaptive or white-box attacks.

title: KCWI Observations of Type 2 Quasar-driven Ionized Outflows at z~0.1
summary: AGN-driven outflows play a crucial role in regulating star formation in galaxies. These outflows are known to be multi-phase, and the characterization of the kinematics, extent, and energetics of each gas phase is needed to obtain a full picture of the outflow properties and impact. This study presents Keck Cosmic Web Imager (KCWI) integral field spectroscopy of the ionized gas outflow properties in seven low redshift (z<0.1) quasars---six Type 2 AGN and one narrow-line Type 1 AGN---providing insight into the warm ionized outflows in these luminous AGN. With the large field-of-view and high sensitivity of KCWI, these data reveal both larger ionized outflow extents than were previously known for these sources and uncover the existence of additional high-velocity kinematic components in the ionized outflows of these luminous AGN. We find (a) a high incidence (50-70%) of multiple outflows on scales of 4--10 kpc and (b) trends between the outflow extent, kinematics, and the ionized mass and energy outflow rates. These trends imply that the faster and often smaller outflows carry higher mass and energy outflow rates than the slower, larger outflows. We also find that the ionized gas outflows reach as far as the known extent of narrow-line ionized gas emission in AGN, which is known to depend weakly on AGN luminosity. This work highlights the utility of the current generation of wide-field integral field spectrographs on 8--10m class telescopes for studying quasar-driven outflows.

title: ActPrune: Action-Grounded Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models perform versatile manipulation tasks from language instructions, but their inference cost limits how fast a robot can respond in closed-loop control. Visual token pruning reduces this cost; however, prior methods estimate token redundancy from encoded visual embeddings or attention, only after the visual encoder has processed the entire observation. We propose \ours, a training-free token pruning method that moves the pruning decision ahead of the vision encoder by grounding it in a geometric prior derived from the robot's own action. The action chunk predicted at the previous control step is already available before the current observation is encoded, and it specifies the end-effector and camera motion between consecutive observations. The same action affects the two standard camera views asymmetrically: in the fixed third-person view, \ours retains patches along the projected end-effector trajectory together with semantic anchors, while in the wrist view, it prunes patches that remain unchanged after compensating for the action-induced camera motion. Extensive experiments on two simulation environments (LIBERO and VLABench) and four real-robot tasks demonstrate that \ours achieves up to 1.61 $\times$ speedup and 59.5\% FLOPs reduction with negligible degradation in success rates.

title: An Ultra-Low-Noise Tunable TIA in 45nm Silicon Photonics for Electro-Optical Ultrasound Data Acquisition
summary: This paper presents the design and experimental characterization of a 32-channel, WDM-compatible electronic-photonic receiver array fabricated in the GlobalFoundries 45nm monolithic silicon photonics process. Optimized for miniaturized, millimeter-scale electro-optical ultrasound data acquisition probes for broadband photo-acoustic imaging (PAI), the chip utilizes integrated micro-ring resonator (MRR) demultiplexers and photodiode (PD) arrays to decode multi-wavelength acoustic signals outside the body. This work focuses specifically on the comprehensive characterization of the receiver front-end, evaluating both the optical WDM filter bank and the transimpedance amplifier (TIA) performance. Monolithic co-integration minimizes critical photodiode-to-TIA interface parasitics. The TIA incorporates a DC-offset cancellation loop that compensates for photodiode-induced offset currents while providing tunable low-frequency cutoff control over a range of 30 kHz to 1.5 MHz. This tunability enables effective suppression of flicker noise and improves overall signal integrity. The front-end achieves the peak transimpedance gain of 144 dB$Ω$ while maintaining an ultra-low input-referred noise current density of $1\text{ pA}/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$, demonstrating a highly scalable architecture for high-sensitivity intravascular and endobronchial imaging.

title: Differential chiral sensing at exceptional points in intrinsically chiral metastructures
summary: Discriminating opposite enantiomers through their weak chiroptical responses remains a fundamental challenge in optical sensing. Exceptional points (EPs), non-Hermitian singularities at which eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, offer a route to enhanced spectral responses through their characteristic square-root eigenvalue splitting. However, their potential for chiral discrimination remains largely unexplored. We demonstrate exceptional points in an intrinsically chiral hybrid metamaterial and reveal strongly asymmetric responses to enantiomeric perturbations. The interplay between intrinsic chirality and non-Hermitian degeneracy is realized through the coupling of a chiral plasmonic nanoantenna array to a photonic crystal slab. We observe characteristic complex-square-root scaling, with both resonance frequencies and loss-rates exhibiting pronounced handedness dependence. Remarkably, opposite enantiomers produce complex mode splittings that differ by more than an order of magnitude. Our findings establish intrinsic chirality as a new degree of freedom in non-Hermitian physics and reveal a fundamental route toward topological singularities enhanced discrimination of chiral matter.

title: Multilevel kernel approximation of log-Euclidean manifold-valued functions
summary: We study kernel approximation and multilevel residual correction for functions with values in a manifold that admits a global logarithm onto a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, such as positive definite matrices, exponential Lie groups, and Hadamard manifolds. Approximating in logarithmic coordinates keeps the approximant on the manifold and transfers Hilbert-space error estimates verbatim. To express these errors in the natural geometry of the target, we prove metric comparisons. In particular, we obtain a sharp, scale-invariant bound between the log-Euclidean and affine-invariant distances on positive definite matrices, with a constant that depends only on condition numbers. For multilevel approximation, compactly supported kernels scaled to the fill distance give algebraic convergence with sparse, uniformly well-conditioned systems. These guarantees require appropriate sample locations and approximation scales. Compact groups are treated through a principal logarithm, where a bi-invariant metric gives error bounds with constant one. Finally, the log-Euclidean and Karcher means differ by $\mathcal O(r^3)$ near the identity and by $\mathcal O(r^2)$ around a general point, where $r$ is the logarithmic data radius and the second bound is sharp.

title: It Takes Two to Tangram: Multi-Agent Object Centric Reinforcement Learning for Assembly
summary: Geometric assembly requires fine spatiotemporal coordination to place parts without causing collisions or deadlocks under tight clearances. To address this, we present an object-centric reinforcement learning framework that treats each part as an agent and learns a shared policy for continuous assembly control. A graph neural network represents the pieces, their target poses, and their spatial relationships, and predicts translational and angular velocities for each component. Per-agent proximal policy optimization with a centralized graph critic directly learns motion and temporal coordination within a single feedback policy. We study this formulation through planar Tangram assembly, where pieces must slide and rotate into a given configuration while remaining on the assembly surface. Procedural generation of target configurations and randomized initial arrangements support training and evaluation across diverse assembly problems. Our experiments isolate the roles of relational structure and multi-agent optimization, and compare learned control with sampling-based planning. We demonstrate concurrent assembly in simulation and transfer the policy to sequential execution on a real robot, as our object-centric formulation decouples learned assembly coordination from low-level physical control. Project page: https://tangrambench.org/

title: Sensing-Based Communication: A Non-Orthogonal Passive Reflection Framework for ISAC
summary: While integrating uplink without disrupting the primary downlink remains a critical challenge for existing reflective communication systems, this paper proposes a non-orthogonal passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) mechanism termed Sensing-based Communication. Originating from and validated within an optical retro-reflective system, this mechanism possesses an underlying wave-agnostic architecture with the potential to be generalized across other physical modalities. It leverages incident downlink signals for parasitic modulation via passive tags. By relying solely on fundamental on-off keying (OOK) reflection, the tag unifies the reflective sensing channel and the uplink communication channel, and simultaneously achieves both sensing and duplex communication. Consequently, our approach introduces uplink capability without sacrificing the downlink data rate or consuming additional spectrum resources. At the receiver, we design a joint decoding architecture combining cross-correlation computation and successive interference cancelation (SIC) to fully exploit the degrees of freedom in broadband signals for multi-user interference suppression. We derive closed-form expressions for the interference and bit error rate (BER) assuming zero-mean Gaussian signals. Using an experimental testbed, we validate the pivotal theoretical finding, the scaling relationship of SINR with signal bandwidth and cross-correlation time--where linear regression yields a strong goodness-of-fit with $R^2 = 0.9688$. Furthermore, evaluations under noise-like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms exhibit high consistency between theoretical derivations and simulation data ($R^2 = 0.9372$, mean absolute percentage error, $\text{MAPE} = 14\%$), confirming the model's accuracy and waveform generalizability.
